'''''Coleus neochilus''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Plectranthus neochilus''''',<ref name=PatoMwanGovaSmit19/> which is colloquially known as '''lobster bush''', '''fly bush''' or '''mosquito bush''', is a perennial [[ground cover]] with highly [[fragrant]], partially scalloped, ovate leaves and  [[Periwinkle (color)|purple blue]] inflorescent spikes.<ref>Codd, L.E. 1975. ''Plectranthus'' (Labiatae) and allied genera in southern Africa. Bothalia 11: 371-442.</ref>

==Description==
The [[succulent]], grey-green leaves present with small hairs on the tops, and a grey-green colour. The plant itself remains a ground cover for the duration of its life (45–60 cm), forming massive bushes rather quickly. The aroma of the plant has been said to resemble [[cannabis]] or [[skunk]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leafly.com/news/lifestyle/cannabis-by-any-other-name-the-israeli-flower-that-smells-like-weed |title=A Bud by Any Other Name: Check Out the Israeli Flower That Smells Like Weed |first=Rae |last=Lland |date=June 20, 2018 |website=Leafly}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hort.net/lists/medit-plants/feb02/msg00119.html|title=Re: Society Garlic |last=Feix |first=David |date=25 February 2002 |website=hort.net|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> They bloom twice a year, in late summer and in late winter.<ref>[https://plantlust.com/plants/12935/plectranthus-neochilus/ Plectranthus neochilus] by Plant Lust</ref>

The specific epithet ''neochilus'' is derived from the Latin word ''chilo'', which refers to the [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]] or lips.<ref>Hankey, A, Joffe, P. & Turner, S. 1999. Water-wise gardening for summer rainfall regions. National Botanical Institute and the Department of Water Affairs and Forestry, Pretoria.</ref>

==Habitat==
The plant is found in dry brush lands, open and sometimes rocky woodland, from the [[Western Cape]], [[Eastern Cape]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[Mpumalanga]] to [[Limpopo]] in [[South Africa]], as well as in [[Zimbabwe]], [[Zambia]] and [[Namibia]].<ref>Van Jaarsveld, E. 1997. Veld gardening in South Africa: the Valley Bushveld/Noorsveld. Veld & Flora 83: 20-25.</ref>

==Cultivation==
Lobster bushes can tolerate wide temperature ranges, dry conditions and almost any soil, but prefer a well-drained sandy loam in full sun or partial shade. Hard [[pruning]] is suggested after flowering. Stems root very readily and the plant extends, where it forms a tidy cluster. Often planted in the landscape of difficult areas, the plant may become a little stressed in very dry conditions, but would revive when it receives some water. 

They can easily be propagated from softwood [[cuttings (plants)|cuttings]] and would multiply in the garden. They are rarely affected by [[Pest (organism)|pests]].<ref>
Van Jaarsveld, E. 1987. The Plectranthus handbook. National Botanic Gardens, Kirstenbosch.</ref>

==Uses==
It is said that this plant can repel [[snake]]s, [[mosquito]]es, flies and most garden pests as a result of its fragrant nature. This makes ''Coleus neochilus'' an ideal companion plant for [[vegetable garden]]s. Furthermore, reports point out that these plants can be used efficaciously as an [[air purifier]].<ref>Van Jaarsveld, E. 1997. Veld gardening in South Africa: the forest garden. Veld & Flora 83: 51-53. Tovhowani Mukoma Lowveld NBG, June 2004</ref>

The dried herb, known as "Falso Boldo" or "boldo-gambá", is employed for treating [[hepatic]] insufficiency and [[dyspepsia]] in folk medicine.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.scielo.br/j/rbfar/a/BjSSFJyVLGnxPZj4KQXq9Pn/?lang=en|title=Stem and leaf anatomy of Plectranthus neochilus Schltr., Lamiaceae|first1=Márcia do Rocio|last1=Duarte|first2=Juliano Ferreira|last2=Lopes|date=December 4, 2007|journal=Revista Brasileira de Farmacognosia|volume=17|pages=549–556|via=SciELO|doi=10.1590/S0102-695X2007000400013|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Tea made by steeping fresh leaves is similar to [[mint herbal tea|mint tea]].<ref>Pooley, E. 1998. A field guide to wild flowers of KwaZulu-Natal and the eastern region. Natal Floral Publications Trust, Durban.</ref>
